To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the standardized EDTA infusion is a valuable tool to study the calcium, phosphate and magnesium homeostasis during the transition from hypercalcaemia to hypocalcaemia in cows.

the standardized EDTA infusion method allows comparison of the response to calcium, phosphate, and magnesium concentrations between two groups of experimental cows, that the response to EDTA infusion is comparable to spontaneous milk fever, that pre-infusion ionized calcium does not correlate with amount of EDTA needed for recumbency, and that the response of total calcium and phosphate to EDTA infusion was different from the response in spontaneous milk fever.

(a) the standardized EDTA infusion procedure allows the study of the response of plasma electrolytes during hypocalcemia in cows; and (b) the response of plasma calcium, inorganic phosphate and magnesium during the infusion is comparable to the response observed during spontaneous hypocalcemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a standardized infusion technique that allows the study of the electrolyte response during hypocalcaemia induced by EDTA infusion.
the development of an in vivo method to study the effect of chelators on calcium metabolism in cattle.
the development of new methods to prevent and treat hypocalcaemia in dairy cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the standardized EDTA infusion method is a useful tool for the experimental study of hypocalcaemia in cows.
a standardized EDTAinfusion technique can be used to induce a hypocalcaemic response in experimental cows that is comparable to that observed in spontaneous milk fever cases.
the standardized EDTA infusion procedure is an effective tool for studying the pathogenesis of hypocalcemia and for evaluating the effects of different treatments on the electrolyte homeostasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intravenous EDTA infusion technique allows effective chelation of calcium and that the response of calcium and phosphate is comparable to that in spontaneous cases of milk fever.
we are working with the development of a new and more efficient method for the treatment of milk fever.

we have demonstrated that it is possible to standardize the Na2EDTAINFUSION TECHNIQUE, so that it is possible in future studies to compare the response of calcium and other electrolytes during the induction of hypocalcaemia in cows.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the standardised EDTA infusion technique allows comparison of the responses of calcium, phosphorous and magnesium between 3 groups of experimental cows and the results obtained were comparable with those in spontaneous milk-fever.
the use of the standardized infusion technique is an important prerequisite to compare the response of calcium and phosphate between groups of cows.
the use of a standardized Na2EDTA intravenous infusion technique allows effective and reproducible hypocalcaemia in cows, which is comparable to that observed in spontaneous cases of milk fever.
